title: Infrastructure Primer
scenario: Welcome to Infrastructure Primer. Before proceeding, you must master these essential networking terms. Power over Ethernet (PoE): IEEE 802.3af (15.4W), 802.3at/PoE+ (30W), 802.3bt/PoE++ (60-100W). Delivers power over UTP to APs, IP phones, cameras. PSE (switch) provides power; PD (device) receives it. Protocol Data Unit (PDU): Generic term for data at each OSI layer. Layer 7-5: Data, Layer 4: Segment (TCP) / Datagram (UDP), Layer 3: Packet, Layer 2: Frame, Layer 1: Bit/Symbol. Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS): Battery backup for power outages. Types: Offline/standby (5-25ms switchover), Line-interactive (AVR, <4ms), Online/Double-conversion (0ms, cleanest power). Sized by VA/watts and runtime. Main Distribution Frame (MDF): Core network room — primary termination point for building cabling. Houses core switches, routers, servers, and WAN connections. IDFs connect back to MDF via vertical/backbone cabling.
question: What does PoE stand for?
explanation: PoE stands for Power over Ethernet.
